name: Argentina
headline: Argentina: +4.5% growth in 2025, 41.9% inflation, debt 80% of GDP
sections: Argentina is a $684 billion economy (2025), the world's 24th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.5% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $33K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 13.6% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 41.9% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, down from 72.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 7.4% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 19.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 80% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 104% in 2020. The general government balance is −0.2% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −1.1% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 30% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.6% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 54% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 77.5 years (2024). Population: 47.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
